taxes.label: Supported Prop 4 (2023) property-tax cut and education-funding amendment (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Led the push for education savings accounts (vouchers), incl. primary campaigns against opponents (Ballotpedia)

cost.label: Campaign: corporations post record profits while Texans pay more; corporate accountability (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Campaign: rein in private equity and insurers 'making healthcare more expensive' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Opposes Abbott's 'voucher scam'; invest in neighborhood public schools (Ballotpedia)

senate.name: Mark Warner
senate.now: U.S. Senator; Vice Chair, Senate Intelligence Committee
senate.background: Virginia's senior senator since 2009 and former governor (2002-2006), who left office with 71% approval. Made a telecom venture-capital fortune before politics. Seeking a fourth term.

cost.label: Focused on 'lowering costs for families, growing wages'; cites $2,900+ in added family costs from tariffs (Senate priorities)

health.label: Early ACA champion who wants to move 'towards a universal coverage model'; defend Medicaid, protect rural hospitals (Senate priorities)

housing.label: Backs bipartisan bills for new construction and first-time-buyer down-payment help; ROAD to Housing Act (Senate priorities)

immigration.label: 'A meaningful pathway to citizenship with secure borders'; DREAM Act; opposes 'inhumane mass round-ups' (Senate priorities)

taxes.label: Wants the wealthiest and corporations 'paying their fair share'; close 'unfair tax loopholes' (Senate priorities)

climate.label: 'All-of-the-above' energy independence: defends offshore wind and nuclear; 'practical, science-based' emissions reduction (Senate priorities)

education.label: College affordability and student-debt relief; industry certifications and non-4-year pathways (Senate priorities)

safety.label: Mixed: prevention plus accountability; body cameras, modern forensics, bipartisan anti-fentanyl work (Senate priorities)

repro.label: Co-introduced the Women's Health Protection Act: decisions 'between a woman and her doctor, not politicians' (Senate release)

democracy.label: Co-sponsor of the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act: 'ensure that every American can make their voice heard' (Senate release)

senate.name: Bert Mizusawa
senate.now: Retired Army Major General; consulting-firm CEO
senate.background: Retired two-star Army general, first in his 1979 West Point class, awarded the Silver Star for a 1984 action at the Korean DMZ. Harvard-trained attorney and former deputy undersecretary of the Army; foreign policy adviser to the 2016 Trump campaign. Won the Aug 4 Republican primary with about 51%.
priorities: Simplify the tax code; attack fraudulent spending

cost.label: Reduce costs for 'farmers, small businesses and working families' through deregulation and American energy (Charlottesville Tomorrow)

immigration.label: Border security plus legal immigration; those 'who broke the law and came here illegally should not be given a free path to citizenship' (Charlottesville Tomorrow)

taxes.label: Simplify tax filing; balance the budget primarily by attacking fraudulent federal spending (Cardinal News)

climate.label: Criticizes energy-production restrictions; supports American energy production; localities should decide on data centers (Charlottesville Tomorrow)

VA-senate.statusNote: Sen. Mark Warner (D), seeking a fourth term, faces retired Army Maj. Gen. Bert Mizusawa (R), who won the Aug 4 primary with about 51%.

governor.name: David Crowley
governor.background: Milwaukee County Executive since 2020, the first Black person and youngest ever elected to the office. Previously served in the Wisconsin State Assembly (2017-2020). Won the Aug 11 Democratic primary in a photo finish over state Rep. Francesca Hong; endorsed by Gov. Tony Evers.

cost.label: Badger Basics plan: $15 minimum wage now and $20 by 2030, cap child-care costs at 7% of income, energy rebates (campaign site)

health.label: Expand BadgerCare with sliding-scale income-based premiums, a public-option approach (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed tools: zoning flexibility for duplexes/fourplexes AND down-payment assistance, eviction prevention, Housing First (campaign site)

immigration.label: Publicly objected to ICE arrests at the Milwaukee County courthouse: they 'undermine public trust, breed fear' (official statement)

climate.label: Led Milwaukee County climate plan (~48% emissions cut, zero-carbon by 2050); wants state investment in solar and retrofits (campaign record)

education.label: Restore two-thirds state school funding, universal early childhood education; would not expand vouchers (Wisconsin Examiner voter guide)

safety.label: Mixed: says the state 'should not defund police' while investing in wraparound services and prevention (Wisconsin Examiner voter guide)

repro.label: 'Access to safe, legal abortion is essential healthcare'; co-sponsored 2017 resolution declaring abortion is health care (official statement)

democracy.label: Supports protecting voting rights and nonpartisan redistricting (campaign plan)

controversies.label: Ran a past Twitter account that posted crude, sexist and homophobic messages (he says he wasn't its sole author), and oversaw a county health-insurance lapse affecting employees, after which he fired the administrator (WPR)

governor.name: Tom Tiffany
governor.background: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 7th District since 2020; before that a state senator, state representative, town supervisor, and river-excursion business co-owner. Won the Aug 11 Republican primary with about 95% of the vote; endorsed by President Trump and Vice President Vance.
priorities: Immigration enforcement; ban sanctuary cities statewide

cost.label: Freeze property taxes, drive down energy costs, cut regulations that raise housing/childcare/health costs (campaign site)

health.label: Backs price transparency and market competition; opposes Medicare for All (Fox6 primary coverage)

housing.label: Cut regulations to make housing more affordable (campaign site)

immigration.label: Ban sanctuary cities statewide, enforce immigration laws, secure the border; opposes amnesty (campaign site)

taxes.label: Property-tax freeze; repeal what he calls Evers' '400-year property tax increase'; touts federal tax cuts (campaign site)

climate.label: Promote baseload power, fight wind/solar projects on farmland; record of opposing environmental regulation (campaign site)

education.label: Focus on reading/writing/math, move money from administration to classrooms, opposes race-based curricula framing (campaign site)

safety.label: More resources for law enforcement; end 'revolving door' policies for repeat offenders (campaign site)

repro.label: Pro-life; supports Wisconsin's existing 20-week abortion ban, calling it a 'compromise'; voted to defund Planned Parenthood as a state legislator (Fox6)

democracy.label: Voted against certifying Arizona's and Pennsylvania's 2020 electoral votes; signed the Texas v. Pennsylvania amicus brief (Wikipedia)

controversies.label: Objected to certifying 2020 electoral votes and signed the Texas v. Pennsylvania brief; one of 14 House votes against the Juneteenth holiday (Wikipedia)
